title: Front Teeth Gap (Diastema): Causes and Treatment Options
seo: Front Teeth Gap (Diastema): Causes & Treatment | Goel Dental
desc: Why gaps between front teeth happen and how they're closed: bonding, veneers, crowns, frenectomy, braces or aligners. By Dr Shikha Goel, Goel Dental.
body:
By Dr Shikha Goel · Cosmetic dentistry

A gap of more than 0.5 mm between the two upper front teeth is called a diastema. Most gaps are harmless and closing them is a personal choice; gaps caused by gum or bone disease need treatment.

When to get it checked

  • The gap makes you self-conscious
  • It has been getting wider
  • Other teeth are spacing too
  • It appeared after an injury
  • Your gums bleed or teeth feel loose

Common causes

  • Jaw and tooth size: teeth small for the jaw
  • Frenum: a band of gum tissue between the front teeth
  • Habits: thumb sucking, tongue thrusting
  • Missing teeth: others drift into the space
  • Gum and bone disease: teeth loosen and move

Ways to close it

OptionVisitsNotes
Bonding1Lowest cost; can stain or chip over 3–5 years
Veneers1–3Some trimming; ceramic resists stains
Crowns2–3Also fix tilted or misshapen teeth
Frenectomy1Removes the frenum, often by laser, with other treatment
Braces or alignersMany monthsMoves the teeth; usually both jaws

If gums or bone are involved, gum treatment comes first.

Technology used at the clinic

  • Digital shade matching
  • CEREC CAD/CAM for same-day bonding, veneers and crowns
  • Biolase soft-tissue laser for frenectomy

title: CAD/CAM Composite Veneers: A Case and What to Know
seo: CAD/CAM Composite Veneers: Case, Time & Cost | Goel Dental
desc: A one-hour CAD/CAM composite veneer case, and how these veneers compare with manual composite and ceramic veneers on look, strength and cost.
body:
By Dr Shikha Goel · CAD/CAM dentistry, cosmetic dentistry

The case

A college student had broken her two upper front teeth in a fall and disliked the composite veneers she received elsewhere. Ceramic veneers were outside her budget, so she chose CAD/CAM composite veneers. The teeth were minimally prepared and scanned; the veneers were designed on screen, approved by her, milled from two composite blocks, then hand-glazed and characterised to match her teeth. The whole case took about an hour.

What CAD/CAM composite veneers are

Veneers milled in the clinic from a factory-made nano-ceramic composite block. They sit between hand-built composite and ceramic veneers on cost and look.

Advantages

  • Better look than hand-built composite
  • Thinner, so more tooth is kept
  • About 15 minutes per veneer to make
  • More shades; picks up fewer stains
  • Can be repaired in the mouth

Limits

  • Less strong than ceramic
  • Lose shine over the years; can be polished

Cost
